title: Catch-Up Payments on Past-Due Northgate Card Accounts
content:
The catch-up payment is the payment a cardholder makes to bring a past-due **Northgate Card Credit Accounts (issued by Harbor Point Bank, N.A.)** account back to good standing; the cardholder makes it in person through the secure payment line, entering there the bank account it is paid from, because representatives never take bank or card numbers.

**Business effect.** The payment is credited to the account as a phone payment dated the day it is made, recorded against the statement whose balance it pays, and lowers the amount the cardholder owes by the amount paid. The cardholder sees the payment on the account and receives a payment confirmation number.

## Invocation: `make_card_payment_5ec32b69`

This is the customer's own action, completed by the customer themselves: no bank or card number passes through the representative. The agent unlocks `make_card_payment_5ec32b69` with `unlock_user_discoverable_tool` and hands it over to the cardholder, who runs it on the secure payment line and enters their own bank details there.

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `card_account_id` | the reference number of the cardholder's Northgate Card account the payment goes to, as the card account lookup returns it and as the representative gives it to the cardholder | id, text |
| `statement_closing_date` | the closing date of the statement whose balance this payment pays | a date written YYYY-MM-DD exactly as the statement shows it |
| `amount_usd` | the payment amount | US dollars, a positive number with 2 decimal places (whole cents) |

The tool applies no rounding: it rejects an amount that is not in whole cents or is zero or below, and a closing date not written YYYY-MM-DD.

**Return.** A text receipt beginning "Payment credited" means the payment is on the account. It gives the 10-digit payment confirmation number, the amount credited, the credit date, the statement closing date the payment is recorded against and the account's new amount owed (negative for a credit balance), amounts in US dollars with two decimals and dates written YYYY-MM-DD.
